title: What should you ask first in a profitability case, and which trap should you avoid?
description: The first question to ask in a profitability case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Profitability cases are the bread and butter of case interviews. If you only prepare one case type properly, make it this one.
body:
The first question to ask

Is the whole industry hit, or just us?

How to build your structure

  • Revenue (units × price, split by product, segment and channel)
  • Costs (fixed vs variable, benchmarked against competitors)

The trap most people fall into

Diagnosing before splitting revenue by product / region / channel.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the profitability framework.

Two prompts to try

A grocer's operating margin fell from 4% to 2% in two years, while sales grew.

Show a model structure
  • Prices and mix: Discounting to match rivals; Shift to lower-margin categories
  • Cost of goods: Supplier prices, shrinkage and waste; Private label share
  • Store costs: Wages, energy, rent; Per store and per $ of sales
  • Online and delivery: Share of sales online; Cost to pick and deliver each order

Where to start: Sales grew but margin halved: find which cost grew faster than sales, as % of sales.

The trap: Talking about growing sales when the problem is margin.

A casual-dining chain's profit per restaurant has halved in three years.

Show a model structure
  • Covers: Guests per restaurant per week; Lunch vs dinner, weekday vs weekend
  • Spend per guest: Menu prices, drinks, desserts; Discounts and vouchers
  • Food and drink costs: Ingredient prices, waste; Menu mix towards low-margin dishes
  • Restaurant costs: Staff hours and wages; Rent, energy, delivery fees

Where to start: Covers first: footfall drops usually drive most of a restaurant's profit fall.

The trap: Blaming food inflation without checking whether fewer people come in.
